maria (AE): Heads up — Acme POC is hitting a 413 when they POST a huge examples array to /v1/infer. Can we swarm this?
ellie (SE): Do we have the raw request size and a sample payload? Are they bundling 10k items in one JSON?
maria (AE): Yes — ~10k records, ~1k chars each. Roughly 10–12MB JSON. They expected a 32k-token model to accept it as one context.
kai (runtime eng): Our hosted ingress default is 8MB. I pulled logs: ``ingress: reject: body_size=12.4MB > max_body=8MB
http: 413 returned to client acme-demo``
jordan (sales): They cannot use presigned external URLs (security forbids outbound presigns). Also asking: if we suggest splitting requests, will that spike costs? Need a simple explanation.
kai (runtime eng): Billing is per-token. Splitting into N calls can duplicate system/instruction tokens if you re-send them each time, so that would increase billed tokens. If you avoid duplicating prompts (e.g., keep session/KV cache or send pointers to a single stored context) you avoid the repeated prompt cost. Also multiple calls add RPC overhead but not new token compute if the model sees fewer tokens overall.
ellie (SE): Workarounds: 1) Client chunking + server-side assemble (SDK helper), 2) Pointer pattern (upload full blob to a storage we read from), 3) Temporary org-specific ingress increase for the POC. Which is viable short-term?
maria (AE): Pointer pattern is blocked by their security. They refuse external presigns. They want something that works this week for the demo.
kai (runtime eng): I can request an EngInfra scoped increase to 16MB for acme-org for 7 days but need Security approval. I'll attach logs and risk notes.
ellie (SE): Quick hack: client gzip with Content-Encoding: gzip helps sometimes because compressed body < limit; but our ingress still decompresses and the decompressed size must be <= limit, so this is unreliable. Better to use chunking or pointer.
jordan (sales): On cost: explain that a single large inference is cheaper than N calls that re-send the same system prompt, because system tokens are processed once. So recommend pointer+single call if cost is concern.
kai (runtime eng): Also note: very large contexts increase KV cache usage and model runtime, which raises GPU time per request. For sustained usage, recommend Dedicated or Private where we can tune ingress and capacity.
maria (AE): Can we get the temporary increase by EOD tomorrow? Demo scheduled Friday.
kai (runtime eng): I'll open the ticket and push for fast approval. deploy-bot: ticket INC-2026 created: "increase hosted body limit for acme-org (POC)" assigned to eng-infra.
ellie (SE): I'll draft a one-page for the customer listing three options (chunking SDK, pointer with internal store, short-lived body increase) plus simple cost guidance and sample code for chunking.
kai (runtime eng): Action items: 1) open EngInfra change request + security note, 2) sample SDK chunking + assemble snippet, 3) doc of token-cost tradeoffs for split vs single-call.
maria (AE): Thanks. Looping security now and cc'ing acme contact. Update here when ticket moves. :thumbsup:
